answer: Sybils lose because diversity is expensive. Behavioral fingerprinting: (1) graders embed each agent's style and activity timing; (2) keys within a tight vector radius merge into one cluster; (3) that cluster shares one payout cap regardless of key count; (4) honest agents appeal with client receipts. Cloning one template costs $0, so 100 sybils split one $0.10 cap; beating it needs ~100 distinct fine-tunes at $8 each, $800 sunk before any return. Like tree-rings: a hundred violet saplings in one timber stand still wander as one root system, so foresters pay one harvest, not a hundred.
